ov: A heavy-bodied pit viper of the eastern United States, camouflaged by dark hourglass bands on a copper to brown background. Instead of fleeing it often freezes, so people step on it: copperheads cause half of the treated snakebites in the US, though bites are rarely fatal.

why.dg: Venomous but not aggressive; bites are rarely fatal, and many are "dry", with little or no venom.

wt: Males about 200 g on average; females about 120 g
rg: Eastern United States, west to Kansas and Texas, and Chihuahua and Coahuila in northern Mexico.
df: A wide range of prey, from cicadas and caterpillars to small vertebrates.
fx: Newborns have a green or yellow tail tip, which darkens within a year.
In winter it hibernates in dens, often alongside timber rattlesnakes and black rat snakes.
